signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.87, holding above its SMA20 at 156.56 while sitting below the SMA50 at 158.77. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard places USD as the top leader with a 1W average of +0.985% across nine pairs, while JPY anchors the laggard position at -0.952% across seven pairs, producing a wide bilateral spread of 1.937%. A 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential, anchored by SOFR at 3.8700% versus TONA at 0.9770%, sustains the structural bid for the greenback against the yen. Options positioning shows an intense put skew with the 25d risk reversal at -2.32, reflecting heavy hedging demand for downside protection as spot grinds higher. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-driven outperformance against the weakest G10 peer. Catalyst: BoJ Trimmed Mean Core CPI y/y release at 05:00 UTC tomorrow. Risk: US 10-year yields reverse sharply below the 5.11% level, triggering a rapid unwind of carry positions.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Late-Trend Caution
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1371, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1562 and SMA50 at 1.1541. Realized volatility over thirty days sits at 4.6% while one-month ATM implied volatility prints at 5.3%, maintaining a modest positive volatility risk premium of +0.7%. The 25-delta risk reversal at -0.51 indicates mild put skew, confirming the options market is hedging downside exposure rather than chasing the recent decline. CFTC leveraged funds maintain a net short position of -51,355 contracts at the 32nd percentile of its 52-week range, though a four-week positive net change of +24,680 contracts shows specs attempting to rebuild short exposure into weakness. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by stalling speculative short additions and entrenched moving-average resistance. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Spot closes back above the SMA20 at 1.1562, invalidating the downside continuation thesis.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Vol
signals.text: GBP/USD changes hands at 1.3225, remaining suppressed below its declining SMA20 at 1.3473 and SMA50 at 1.3476. One-month implied volatility stands at 5.4% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.8%, yielding a +0.7% volatility risk premium that mirrors the broader dollar-bloc defensive posture. Leveraged funds hold a net long position of +18,698 contracts at the 60th percentile of its 52-week range, accompanied by a sharp four-week reduction of -27,372 contracts that highlights aggressive long liquidation. Price action remains weighed down by the broader greenback strength while options skew reflects mild put demand with the 25d risk reversal at -0.54. Trade bias: Short GBP/USD, vulnerable to further long liquidation as moving averages cap recovery attempts. Catalyst: BoE Governor Bailey speech at 09:15 UTC. Risk: Spot reclaims the SMA20 cluster at 1.3473, halting the liquidation cycle.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7027, hovering near its SMA200 at 0.7022 while sitting well below the SMA20 at 0.7157. Leveraged funds maintain a large net long position of +59,299 contracts, placing positioning at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +2.11σ. The four-week net change shows steady accumulation at +9,550 contracts, maintaining a crowded long footprint despite spot sliding 1.25% over the past week. Options reflect moderate put skew with the 25d risk reversal at -0.79, while the economic surprise index sits at +9.4, failing to provide fresh upside momentum for the currency. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD, highly vulnerable to a sharp long-unwind squeeze given extreme positioning against deteriorating spot momentum. Catalyst: Australia CFTC non-commercial net positions release at 19:30 UTC. Risk: Spot breaks cleanly below the SMA200 at 0.7022, triggering accelerated stop-losses from crowded longs.
